dialogue_lines_reviewed.text: Hi! Let's count prime numbers.
A prime number is a whole number greater than one with exactly two positive factors: one and itself.
A factor divides a number evenly, with nothing left over.
Let's try five tiles.
Five makes one row of five. Its only factors are one and five.
Six also makes two rows of three. Six has more than two factors, so it is not prime.
Turning a rectangle around does not give us new factors.
One has only one factor: one. So one is not prime.
Now let's count every prime number below one thousand.
Two has exactly two factors: one and two.
Any larger even number has two as another factor.
Two is the only even prime.
Nine is odd, but three rows of three make nine.
Nine has factors other than one and itself. It is not prime.
Ninety-eight, ninety-nine, and one hundred have extra factors.
The next prime after ninety-seven is one hundred one.
We did it!
We counted all one hundred sixty-eight prime numbers below one thousand.
The last one was nine hundred ninety-seven.
Thanks for counting with me. Bye for now!

title: Prime Numbers 2 to 997 | Count All 168 Primes Below 1000 | Num-Num Numbers
description:
Count every prime number below 1,000 with our kangaroo guide at the Sunlit Mosaic Museum!

We count 168 prime numbers from 2 to 997 in natural American English, with a calm pace and large, clear numbers. Tile exhibits introduce factors, show why 1 and 9 are not prime, and explain why 2 is the only even prime. Near 100, we look at why the next prime after 97 is 101.

A prime is a whole number greater than 1 with exactly two positive factors: 1 and itself. One tile in the finished mosaic stands for one prime we counted.

No background music or sound effects.
